question: Can the s107 'multistart inside the cross filter' delivery plan (drop C-pass, rank multistart roots by coarse-K full-LC RMSE) surface truth-near pairs blind AND meet the 15-min/seed budget on aliased seed 119?
hypothesis: Multistart inside the cross filter, ranked by coarse-K RMSE, can deliver a truth-near seed to the polish at production scale within the 15-min/seed budget.
narrative_md: The s107 delivery plan is dead: Stage 0 showed C-pass rejects 0/23 multistart roots of the s106 oracle pair (truth-near root only fits brightness post-polish). The redesign -- drop C-pass, rank by coarse-K full-LC RMSE -- WORKS as a blind, phantom-free discriminator (6 Band A, 0 phantoms on a 1675-pair subsample; oracle reproduces s106 0.0300 via a fully blind path). BUT it cannot meet the 15-min budget: dropping C-pass leaves 3.17M survivors, multistart needs n_dir=16 to find the winding (71.5 hr full run), coarse cross at deg=10 is 65 min and drifts to 4.4 deg -- ~100x over budget. Bankable: the coarse-K-on-best-winding-root discriminator is clean. Redirect to the anchor-baseline-aliasing blocker. Stage 0 uses the oracle pair + truth labels (oracle-leak); N=1.
